The main takeaway from our work is that

in patients with ITP undergoing major joint surgery, a combination of preoperative platelet transfusion, intraoperative cell salvage and autotransfusion, and postoperative antiplatelet therapy can be used to achieve a successful outcome.
in a patient with a low platelet count who has a history of ITP, a preoperative platelet count of 20 × 109/L is a reasonable cut-off to proceed with a major joint replacement.
patients with chronic ITP and low platelet count can safely undergo major joint replacement surgery with careful preoperative preparation and close monitoring during the perioperative period.
